e.etymology: The Spanish and Italian spelling of Ophelia, probably from Greek opheleia, help or benefit. Shakespeare made the name famous through the tragic heroine of Hamlet.
namesakes: Ofelia (the girl at the center of the film Pan's Labyrinth)

assoc.t: Ophelia, tragic heroine of Hamlet (spelled Ophelia)

e.etymology: An Afrikaans feminine form of Charles, built with the South African name ending -ize. Charles goes back to Germanic karl, free man. Actress Charlize Theron carried the name to the United States.
namesakes: Charlize Theron (Oscar-winning actress in Monster and Mad Max: Fury Road)

assoc.t: actress Charlize Theron

e.etymology: Used in the United States mostly by African American families, and in Jamaica. Its source is uncertain. Damani is also a Gujarati surname from India.
A modern American coinage that runs the phrase a miracle together into one name, in the pattern of Amira and Amari.
An Arabic form of Joseph, from Hebrew Yosef, he will add. Yusuf is a prophet in the Quran, and its twelfth chapter tells his story.
A modern American coinage with the sound of Ayden, Evan and Avery. It has no established meaning.
A pet form of Susan and Susanna, from Hebrew Shoshannah, lily. It was widely given as a full name in the late 1800s.

assoc.t: Wake Up Little Susie, 1957 Everly Brothers hit

e.etymology: A spelling of Darrell, an English surname brought by the Norman d'Airel family, who took their name from Airelle in Calvados, France.
namesakes: Daryl Hall (singer of Hall and Oates)
Daryl Hannah (actress in Splash and Kill Bill)

assoc.t: Daryl Dixon of The Walking Dead

e.etymology: A spelling of Arabic Husayn, a diminutive of Hasan, from the root h-s-n, good or beautiful. Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, is revered above all by Shia Muslims.

assoc.t: Saddam Hussein, Iraqi dictator (spelled Hussein)

e.meaning: end of the Vedas, ultimate knowledge
e.etymology: From Sanskrit vedanta, literally the end of the Vedas: the name given to the Upanishads and to the school of Hindu philosophy built on them.

assoc.t: Adam Sandler's You Don't Mess with the Zohan (2008 film)

e.note: Many Americans know the name from the 2008 Adam Sandler comedy You Don't Mess with the Zohan.

e.etymology: An English surname from the town of Derby, from Old Norse djur, deer, and byr, settlement. In Ireland Darby was also used as an English stand-in for Diarmaid.
namesakes: Darby O'Gill (hero of Disney's Darby O'Gill and the Little People)

e.etymology: From an English place name and surname: the River Lea plus Old English tun, settlement. It is often treated as a spelling of Leighton or Layton.
The medieval English form of Benedict, from Latin benedictus, blessed. It became a surname, more often spelled Bennett, and has come back into use as a first name.

assoc.t: the Bennet family in Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice

e.etymology: From Greek rhema, an utterance or thing said. In Christian teaching, especially in Pentecostal and charismatic churches, rhema is the word of God spoken directly to a believer.

assoc.t: Rhema Bible Training College and Rhema churches

e.etymology: A respelling of Ace, the playing card and the word for someone who excels, from Latin as, a unit.
e.note: AYCE is common shorthand for all-you-can-eat on restaurant signs and menus.

e.etymology: The everyday Spanish form of Isidoro, from Greek Isidoros, gift of Isis. San Isidro Labrador, a farm laborer from Madrid, is the patron saint of farmers.
A spelling of Malcolm, from Scottish Gaelic Maol Chaluim, devotee of Saint Columba. Four kings of Scotland bore the name.

assoc.t: civil rights leader Malcolm X (spelled Malcolm)
Malcolm in the Middle sitcom (spelled Malcolm)

e.note: Most people will spell it Malcolm, so expect to correct the spelling often.

e.meaning: Ta-Ha, the two letters that open the 20th chapter of the Quran
e.etymology: From the Arabic letters ta and ha, which open the 20th surah of the Quran and give it its name. Their meaning is not known; many Muslims take Taha as a name of the Prophet Muhammad.
In American use a respelling of Elias, the Greek form of Elijah, from Hebrew Eliyahu, my God is Yahweh. Alias is also the Malay form of Ilyas, the Arabic name of the same prophet.

assoc.t: the English word alias, an assumed or false name
Alias, ABC spy series with Jennifer Garner

e.note: Spelled like the English word alias (an assumed name), usually said AY-lee-us, so expect jokes and mispronunciation.

e.etymology: A short form of Brianna and Breanna that came into use on its own in the 1970s. It sounds the same as Brie, the French cheese.
namesakes: Bree Van de Kamp (Desperate Housewives character)

assoc.t: sounds like Brie, the French soft cheese
Bree, village in The Lord of the Rings

e.etymology: A short form of Alexander or Aleksander, from Greek alexo, to defend, and aner, man. The k spelling is the usual one in Polish.
A form of Shiva, from Sanskrit shiva, the auspicious one, the name of one of the principal Hindu gods. Shiv is also a nickname for the Irish name Siobhan.
namesakes: Shiv Roy (Siobhan Roy, character on HBO's Succession)

assoc.t: shiv, slang for a makeshift knife
Shiv Roy of HBO's Succession

e.note: In American English a shiv is a makeshift knife, especially one made in prison.

e.etymology: A modern blend of Ana, a form of Hannah (Hebrew for grace), and the Biblical name Leah. It is also heard as a spelling of Analia.
e.note: The spelling begins with the letters anal, which can draw teasing in English-speaking schools.

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that joins Ana to the -liyah ending of Aaliyah. It can also be read as an elaborated spelling of Analia.
e.note: The spelling begins with the letters anal, which can draw teasing in English-speaking schools.

e.etymology: From Arabic ruh, soul or spirit: ruhi means of the soul, or my soul. In India and Pakistan it is a girl's name, while in Turkey and the Arab world Ruhi is given to boys.
From the spring flower, whose name comes from medieval Latin prima rosa, first rose. One of the Victorian flower names, it returned with Primrose Everdeen of The Hunger Games.
namesakes: Primrose Everdeen (Katniss's younger sister in The Hunger Games)

assoc.t: Prim, Katniss's sister in The Hunger Games
Primrose Schools, national preschool chain

e.etymology: A modern American name that crosses Everly with Evelyn and takes the -lynn ending of Adalynn and Brooklynn.
A Spanish-language pet form of María, and sometimes of Marta, in wide use across Latin America.
From the Irish surname O Diomasaigh, descendant of Diomasach, a byname from diomasach, proud.
namesakes: Jack Dempsey (heavyweight boxing champion of the 1920s)

assoc.t: actor Patrick Dempsey and boxer Jack Dempsey (surname)

e.etymology: A spelling of Max, the short form of Maximilian and Maxwell. Maximilian comes from Latin maximus, greatest.
namesakes: Maxx Crosby (Las Vegas Raiders defensive end)

assoc.t: T.J. Maxx, discount clothing and home store chain

e.etymology: A modern American elaboration of Xavier with the -ian ending of Damian and Julian. Xavier comes from the Basque place name Etxeberria, new house.
